findings.passage: "Under my bill it is simple. All you need is a photo ID. Period," Obenshain told CBS 6 reporter Joe St. George.
findings.note: Quoted by WTVR (CBS 6) about his SB 1256 photo ID bill; the same story quotes him saying a voter without a photo ID could get one free at the local registrar's office.
subjects: free state ID for voters without ID

findings.passage: In the Democratic Party-run firehouse primary to choose the party’s state senate nominee in the 16th District special election, Democrats — free to adopt any voter identification standard they wished, or none at all — opted for requirements considerably more stringent than those contained in the state law they denounce, actually going so far as to require that IDs show the address at which the individual is registered.
findings.note: From his 2014-08-13 newsletter as quoted by PolitiFact (published 2014-09-09); he argues a private primary used ID rules stricter than state photo ID law.

findings.passage: There is no evidence that photo ID ever suppressed a single vote – except perhaps fraudulent ones.
findings.note: His newsletter criticising the 2020 law repealing Virginia's photo ID requirement; it also calls that repeal bill 'particularly troubling'.

findings.passage: Last week, the Privileges and Elections Committee heard multiple election integrity bills. Notwithstanding broad bipartisan support, the Committee refused to reinstate the photo ID mandate.
findings.note: His 2023 session newsletter; also says the committee rejected a bill ending same-day registration and one criminalising intentional efforts to register non-citizens to vote.

findings.passage: “There are people out there who believe that there are big gaping holes in our system,” Obenshain said. “This just is a common-sense way to address those concerns.”
findings.note: Quoted by WTOP at the committee hearing where his bill to require photo ID at the polls failed; story says he said he was not trying to suggest epidemic fraud.

findings.passage: “Over the course of this past year, of course, Americans have been asked to show proof of vaccination, even in order to be able to work. So this is simply restoring the requirement of showing the identification.
